thread_pair_example: driver, 20000 items: grid 20 x 1024 threads, dynamic shared 80 bytes. Block 0, thread 991 (warp 30) stores the final co[1023] at L77 (the L75 loop gives thread t the element i = t + 32; thread 1023 has no L77 iteration because 1023 + 32 >= 1024); the earlier partial value of co[1023] was stored at L22 by thread 1023 (L60 loop, i = t); the block B whose thread 0 gets value == 19 from atomicAdd(pc,1) at L155 (the last one to finish; any blockIdx) runs, in its thread 0, i = 0: j = blockDim.x*0 + 1023, loads co[1023] at L172. There is no __threadfence() before the atomicAdd in block 0 and no acquire after it in block B, and nothing else orders them (different blocks): global RAW. (driver, 2000 items: grid 2 x 1024: the same pair when block 1 finishes last.)
class_reason: In the buggy program co and ci are plain pointers: every access to co is an ordinary LDG.E / STG.E (no volatile, no .STRONG token, no atomic); the only atomic is the block counter pc (ATOMG.E.ADD.STRONG.GPU, L155) which is not the data. A conflicting pair of two plain accesses with no happens-before edge (no fence on either side of the counter handoff) is a data race (DR), not SC.
buggy_expected: The pair (L77 store of block b vs L172 load by the last-done block) is reported as DR (global RAW across blocks). Also expected as DR in the same kernel (extra_pairs): the L22 store vs the L172 load, and the L22/L77 stores of other blocks vs the last block's L179 read-modify-write (RAW and WAW across blocks).

residual_sites.operation: st.volatile.global (SASS: STG.E.STRONG.SYS [R4.64], R9 at 0x0740; co is now volatile T*)

fixed.reason: UNCERTAIN, taken from verify.expected_report_fixed. The fix makes ci/co volatile (all accesses become strong: LDG.E.STRONG.SYS / STG.E.STRONG.SYS) and puts __threadfence() (L157, SASS MEMBAR.SC.GPU; ERRBAR; CCTL.IVALL at 0x07c0-0x0800) before the counter atomicAdd (L158, ATOMG.E.ADD.STRONG.GPU), i.e. a release pattern on the writing side. The last-done block has NO fence after its atomicAdd (only the block barrier BAR.SYNC at L162 and the strong loads), so by the formal PTX model there is no acquire pattern and the strong-vs-strong conflict is not ordered: the formal expectation is a residual of class SC on the same pair (moved to L77 / L175 in the fixed file). A detector that accepts 'fence; atomic' as a complete handoff (the CUDA threadFenceReduction idiom) reports nothing, so 'absent' is also a legitimate outcome; the pair is therefore recorded as residual with this caveat and listed in open_questions.

Fixed: every co/ci access is LDG.E.STRONG.SYS / STG.E.STRONG.SYS (L14 0x0170, L22 0x0360, L77 0x06c0/0x0740, L175 0x09b0, L182 0x1090/0x10f0, plus a LDG.E.STRONG.SYS at L66 0x0380 that re-reads co[i] for ws[warpId]), MEMBAR.SC.GPU; ERRBAR; CCTL.IVALL at 0x07c0-0x0800 (the __threadfence at L157) directly before ATOMG.E.ADD.STRONG.GPU (0x0820); no fence after the atomic in the last block. YIELD instructions appear next to the volatile accesses (fixed only). No WARPSYNC. T_RACECHECK=na (global memory).

open_questions: Fixed side: whether a detector must report the volatile pair as SC (formally no acquire pattern in the last block) or may accept the fence + atomic handoff is not settled by the sources; verify.expected_report_fixed is 'uncertain'. Both outcomes are possible; the draft registers 'residual' (SC) as the formal reading.

Which block is the 'last block done' is timing dependent (the block whose atomicAdd returns gridDim.x-1), so the thread/block ids in thread_pair_example are one instance of the pair, not fixed ids; a dynamic detector sees the pair for whichever block finishes last.

review.notes: R2 harness: every copied kernel file under r2/buggy and r2/fixed is byte-identical (cmp) to git show <buggy_commit>:<path> / <fix_commit>:<path>; git diff buggy..fix of those files is exactly the fix hunk described in fixed.reason. (prefixScan.h, cudaCompat.h, cudaCheck.h, cuda_assert.h; the fix diff touches prefixScan.h and cudaCompat.h, the latter only a host-side atomicCAS emulation). Buggy pair confirmed: co is a plain T* in multiBlockPrefixScan (prefixScan.h:141); block b's final store co[i] at L77 and the last-done block's load co[j] (j = 1024*i + 1023) at L172 are in different blocks; the only cross-block operation is atomicAdd(pc, 1) at L155 with no __threadfence on either side, so plain/plain unordered -> DR. Driver: separate d_in / d_out1 buffers (driver.cu:41-42,57), so the ci reads (L14) do not alias co. extra_pairs (L22 vs L172; L22/L77 vs the last block's RMW at L179) confirmed. The device-side asserts (L144, L146, L164 '*pc') are compiled out: cuda_assert.h defines NDEBUG under __CUDA_ARCH__ unless GPU_DEBUG is set, and the nvcc line of target.sh does not set it, so the plain read of *pc at L164 is not an extra pair. Fixed (d1ce91e): ci/co volatile (L142-143), __threadfence() at L157 before the atomicAdd at L158 in thread 0, after the block barrier L79 of blockPrefixScan; the last-done block has no fence after its own atomicAdd before the volatile loads at L175 (only the barrier L162), so under PTX there is a release pattern but no acquire pattern and the strong/strong conflict stays unordered: the registered SC residual (L77 vs L175) is the strict reading, 'absent' the idiomatic one, as open_questions[0] says. The same holds for the extra pair in the fixed file (L77 or L22 vs the RMW at L182, both volatile): if the primary residual is reported, expect this one too. depends_on_D20 = false: the scored buggy pair is plain/plain (DR); the fixed-build SC residual is a release/acquire question, not a D20 question.
